title: The Canapé Rule
logline: When Victoria's waitstaff quits hours before she caters the book launch of a food critic who reviews everything in one word, she drafts the gang as emergency staff, with one rule: waiters are furniture. Ted can't stop lecturing the guests or planning a forty-one-slide tribute to her, Barney turns the invisible uniform into a play, and when Marshall eats the critic's one perfect bite, saving Victoria's night means Ted has to do the hardest thing he's ever done for a woman: listen.
coldOpen: Kids, in the fall of 2012, I prepared the greatest toast of my life. Forty-one slides, a cross-section and a tiny laser pointer. I never said a word of it.

couch.line: Let me guess. It was for a woman who isn't Mom.
Penny, this is a story about the hospitality industry.

guests.name: Cornelia Vance
guests.role: Restaurant critic at the New York Ledger for thirty-seven years, famous for one-word reviews that make or end careers; speaks almost entirely in single words, and turns out to be a torrential talker the moment anyone asks her a follow-up question

guests.name: Margaux Pell
guests.role: Cornelia's publicist, a rapid-fire oversharer who tells waiters everything because waiters don't count; Barney's mark, who talks to him for two hours about her boss and never once asks his name

scenes.summary: Victoria's van died on the Williamsburg Bridge, so Ted sends Barney's limo and the whole gang as emergency waitstaff. Victoria climbs in up front beside Ranjit and briefs them through the partition: the critic Cornelia Vance reviews in one word, and one good word makes her business. Assignments: Robin on bar, Lily on coats (no pockets), Marshall on tiny food, and a single perfect cream puff that nobody touches. Rule one: waiters are furniture. Barney unveils the Invisible Man play; Ted's canapé etymology gets him told to be the couch. Victoria jumps out to run the last block, and Ted reveals his secret forty-one-slide toast. Button: a couch with a slideshow is a TV.

beats.line: That fall, Victoria and I were off again. Then her catering van died on the Williamsburg Bridge.
Ted, when I called you, I was hoping for a jump start. Not a limo and five waiters.
Six, counting Ranjit.
Hello! I am also catering.
Here's the situation. My entire waitstaff quit this morning. They all got cast in the same off-Broadway musical.
It's about waiters.
Victoria, I have never worn a vest without a jacket. I look like a suit that gave up halfway.
Tonight is the book launch for Cornelia Vance. Restaurant critic at the Ledger, thirty-seven years. She reviews everything in one word.
One word. Like, yum?
Like damp. That's what she gave the caterer at the Plaza. He lives in Delaware now.
So what's the word you want?
Any good one. One good word, and I stop being a bakery that caters. I'm a caterer with a bakery. With a second location.
That's a lot of weight on one word.
Which is why I'm in a limo full of amateurs. Robin, you're on bar. Signature cocktail, the Fine. After her book.
Scotch, neat, garnished with more scotch.
Lily, coat check.
Yes! You learn everything about a person from their coat.
You do not go in the pockets.
Who goes in pockets?
Marshall, tiny food.
Tiny food!
And at nine, one cream puff goes out on a silver plate, for Cornelia only. Cardamom, brown butter, salted honey.
Three weeks I worked on that puff. Nobody touches it.
I heard you, Victoria. I want you to know I heard you.
What was the one after brown butter?
Barney, Ted, you're waiters. Rule one: waiters are furniture. Nobody looks at you. Nobody remembers you.
Wait. Nobody looks at the waiter?
People will say things in front of you they wouldn't tell their priest.
She tells the furniture her type. The furniture becomes her type.
beats.title: The Invisible Man
lines: Overhear exactly what she wants in a man.
Be exactly what she wants in a man.

beats.line: When do you change into the suit?
He doesn't. He's in that vest until midnight.
Then I will be the sexiest furniture in Manhattan.
It's fitting, actually. Did you know canapé is French for couch? Because the topping sits on the bread like a man on a—
Ted. Tonight, you are the couch. Couches don't explain themselves.
Not even a little etymology?
Especially not the etymology.
Ranjit, stop here. I'll run the last block. My feet are faster than Midtown.
Good luck, Miss Victoria! Do not worry about the croquembouche. I will drive it like it is my mother.
Okay, she's gone. Nobody tell her, but at dessert, I'm giving a toast.
Forty-one slides. Each one more moving than the last.
beats.title: Victoria: A Structural Appreciation
lines: Slide 9: My thesis on flying buttresses

beats.line: Ted, she just told you to be a couch.
Then I'll be a couch with a slideshow.
That's a TV, Ted.

scenes.summary: The launch party at Brasserie Delacroix. Ted lectures Margaux about plaster while she waits for a napkin; Victoria hisses 'Couch.' Marshall is sitting in a booth eating his own tray. Robin serves scotch to everyone. Lily did not go through Cornelia's pockets, but has her notebook: 'Tall waiter: no.' Cornelia stops Ted's aqueduct lecture with one word and orders scotch neat; Robin is in love. Barney's play works too well: Margaux has told him everything, about her boss. Lily warns Ted that speeches get the word 'Loud'; Ted's imagined toast is a triumph. Button: Victoria asks who moved the silver plate, and we freeze on Marshall.

beats.line: Cornelia's launch party was at Brasserie Delacroix. Her memoir was called Fine. It was nine hundred pages long.
And that ceiling is original 1904 plaster. Egg-and-dart molding. The egg symbolizes life, and the dart, of course—
I asked for a napkin. Twenty minutes ago. I've been using my sleeve.
Couch.
Couch.
Marshall. Why are you sitting in a booth?
Victoria, these are incredible. Every one is a whole dinner that got shrunk. I'm a giant at a tiny banquet.
You're a waiter in a booth.
A waiter who believes in the product.
Lily, a man in a turtleneck just asked me for a mojito.
What did you give him?
Scotch and a look.
Robin. I did not go through anybody's pockets.
Lily.
But if I had, Cornelia Vance carries a notebook. And she's already started on tonight's words.
What does it say?
Canapés, pending. Bar, pending. Tall waiter, no.
Ms. Vance, good evening. Some water? Ours comes from the Catskills, through an aqueduct completed in nineteen—
Stop.
Stopping.
Scotch.
Neat?
Obviously.
Lily. I think I just met my soulmate, and she's sixty-eight.
Your napkin, madam.
Oh thank God, you again. Waiters don't count, so where was I? Right. Cornelia and the mayor of Lyon.
Ted, it's working. Two hours. She's told me everything.
About what she wants in a man?
About her boss. I know Cornelia's blood type. I don't know Margaux's last name.
Ted. The notebook has a whole page on toasts. Anyone who makes a speech gets one word. Loud.
Mine isn't a speech. It's a structural appreciation. When I'm done, there won't be a dry eye in the room.
Ladies and gentlemen. Slide twelve. The croquembouche. A load-bearing dessert.
Magnificent.
I'm not crying. I'm just very moved by the buttresses.
Ted Mosby. Architect. Of my heart.
Ted, she reviewed her own wedding. One word. Long.
That's because nobody gave her a cross-section.
Okay, people! Twenty minutes to the perfect bite. Who moved the silver plate?
Kids, your Uncle Marshall has done a lot of things he's not proud of. That was the most delicious one.

scenes.summary: The service elevator down to Delacroix's kitchen. Marshall confesses: the puff looked lonely. Victoria needs twenty-five minutes to make another, and Cornelia leaves every party at nine. Ted offers to stall her with the toast, but Lily already told Victoria about the slides (and the dishwasher). Victoria says what she needs: for the room to taste it and find out on their own, or it isn't hers. She takes Marshall to pipe, no licking. Barney, who has spent two hours listening, gives Ted the solution: nobody has asked Cornelia a follow-up question since 1987. Ask one, then shut up. Be the couch. Button: she says expresso.

beats.line: Three weeks, Marshall. Cardamom. Brown butter. Salted honey.
It was all alone on a silver plate, Victoria. It looked so lonely.
I gave it a home.
A new one takes twenty-five minutes. Cornelia leaves every party at nine, and reviews whatever she's tasted by then.
Right now, that's one scotch and a lecture about an aqueduct.
I can stall her. I happen to have something prepared. It opens with a slide that—
The slides? Lily told me. Lily told me before I asked. Lily told the dishwasher.
It's a tribute! Forty-one slides!
Slide nine is your thesis, Ted.
It sets up slide ten.
Slide twelve is a cross-section of my croquembouche. With my face on it.
To scale!
Ted. I don't need somebody to tell that room I'm good. I need them to taste it and find out on their own.
Otherwise it isn't mine. It's yours, about me.
I just wanted everybody to see you.
Then let them see the food. You make that speech, she writes loud, and I'm doing birthday cupcakes in Delaware.
Let me help. I'm very good with food.
Marshall, you are the reason we're in this elevator.
You're on piping. If you lick the bag, you're fired.
That's fair.
How do I keep a woman who speaks in one word at that table for twenty-five minutes, without a speech?
Easy. Do what I've been doing all night.
Hitting on her publicist?
Listening.
Margaux says nobody has asked Cornelia a follow-up question since 1987. Ask her one, Ted. Then shut up.
For twenty-five minutes?
The canapé rule, Ted. Be the couch.
But what if she's wrong about something? What if she mispronounces something?
Then you let her be wrong.
Barney, I have never let anyone be wrong. I corrected the doctor who delivered me.
Two hours ago, I'd have said I couldn't listen either. Turns out I'm a fantastic listener. Nobody knew, because I never shut up.
Oh, and Ted? She says expresso.
With an X?
So many X's.

scenes.summary: Cornelia asks for her coat; Lily says it's in transit. Ted, holding a water glass he swears isn't for tapping, sits with Cornelia and asks why one word. She talks: the soufflé, the editor, and the state of expresso in this city. Ted lets it go, twice. Marshall, fired for licking the bag, delivers the new bite untouched. Cornelia asks who made it; Ted puts down the glass and says the chef, Victoria. Cornelia's word: Again. Robin gets 'Correct' twice; Ted gets 'Tall'. Alone, Victoria lets Ted finish his canapé lecture: nobody notices the bread. She noticed. Honest: it's a thank-you, not a sign, and she won't have a free Saturday for two years. Barney gets tipped and booked as a wedding waiter. Future Ted: the column ran, plus a footnote: Listens.

beats.line: Coat.
Absolutely! Your coat is currently in transit.
Transit.
Ted. Why are you holding an empty glass?
It's for emergency tapping.
Ms. Vance. May I ask you one question?
One.
Why only one word?
Nobody has asked me that since 1987.
Sit.
My first review was eight hundred words. Seven hundred and ninety of them were about one soufflé.
My editor cut it to one. Collapsed. Best thing I ever wrote. I've been chasing that word for thirty-seven years.
He's been listening for twelve minutes. I didn't know his face could do that.
And do you know what's wrong with this city, waiter? Nobody makes a proper expresso.
Mm-hm.
A real expresso. With a lemon peel. Like in Rome. Expresso.
Go on.
Dad. Tell me you didn't correct her.
I didn't, Penny. I bit my tongue so hard, for a week I couldn't say espresso either.
It's ready. Marshall, you carry it. Yours are the only hands in this building that aren't shaking.
Your perfect bite, ma'am.
I didn't eat it. I want that on the record. I licked the bag, and I got fired, but I did not eat it.
Who made this?
The chef. Victoria.
Again.
Thank you.
Don't push it.
Found your coat!
Bar. Correct.
Lily. Nine years in news, and nobody has ever called me correct.
Waiter.
Yes?
Tall.
Robin, Marshall. Help me find the other coats I hid.
You didn't do the slides.
Forty-one of them. Slide twelve was to scale.
Ted. Do you know what canapé means?
You're going to let me answer?
Just this once.
It's French for couch! Because the topping sits on the bread, the way a man sits on a couch!
And?
And the bread holds everything up. And nobody notices the bread.
I noticed the bread.
I'm the bread.
And you're making it weird.
So does this mean we're—
Ted. It's not a sign. It's a thank-you. If that word runs Sunday, I won't have a free Saturday for two years.
Then go be booked. I'll be the guy who says he knew you when.
You'll be the guy who says he worked for me. For one night. And was terrible at it.
Ted! Margaux tipped me forty dollars and booked me for her sister's wedding. Thirty bridesmaids, and to every one of them, I'm furniture.
You're going to be a wedding waiter?
It is going to be legen... I'll be right with you... dary!
Sunday's column gave Victoria one word: Again. One waiter got a footnote: Listens. I had it framed. Your mother has requested a correction.
